key_insight: LLM-based radiology report metrics should separate true clinical errors from harmless wording changes, because current evaluators tend to over-penalize rephrasings.
clinical_relevance: A sharper clinical-significance boundary can improve automated evaluation of generated radiology reports, helping prioritize omissions or misstatements that could affect patient care.
method: Tested 8 LLM evaluators on the ReEvalMed benchmark.
Measured two metric behaviors: discrimination of true errors and robustness to insignificant variation.
Trained lightweight interpretable metrics on 4k synthesized report pairs using Qwen3-8B and MedGemma-4B.
evidence_signal: Across one-pass and two-pass settings, the study found a widespread discrimination bias: evaluators detected errors but often misclassified harmless rephrasings as clinically important.
watch_item: Two-pass inference did not consistently improve overall performance, so deployment should weigh added cost against only partial gains in the discrimination-robustness balance.
paper_title: Beyond Scalar Scores: Exploring LLM-based Metrics for Clinical Significance Evaluation in Radiology Reports
